recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up is needed for FHIR-14147 in core FHIR unless a future work group decision changes the ImagingStudy subject or specimen model.
issue_request: FHIR-14147 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution for STU3 ImagingStudy. It requested renaming ImagingStudy.patient to subject, adding Device and Group as subject target types alongside Patient, and representing whole-slide imaging specimens with a new series-level 0..* Reference(Specimen) element instead of adding Specimen to the study subject.
initial_application: Git commit d21acd48143d1cbe35a35616864c97839b13a361 explicitly mentions GF#14147 and changed the old ImagingStudy spreadsheet/examples from patient to subject, set the subject type to Reference(Patient|Device|Group), and added ImagingStudy.series.specimen. Later source refactors moved the authoritative definition into source/imagingstudy/structuredefinition-ImagingStudy.xml.
additional_context: ImagingStudy is active in source/fhir.ini. The current StructureDefinition has ImagingStudy.subject as 1..1 Reference(Patient, Device, Group), with the QA phantom Device and Group semantics in the comment, and has ImagingStudy.series.specimen as 0..* Reference(Specimen). The retained ImagingStudy-patient search parameter intentionally filters ImagingStudy.subject to Patient while ImagingStudy-subject covers the broader reference; later search-parameter issue FHIR-32876 supports Patient-only patient-scoped search targets. Corrected Zulip and Confluence searches found no direct FHIR-14147 discussion or conflicting community evidence.
reconciliation: No source edit was needed. Adding Specimen to ImagingStudy.subject or broadening the legacy patient search parameter would contradict the modified resolution and later search-parameter context.

related_jiras.note: Later published search-parameter issue, duplicate of FHIR-31714, supporting patient-scoped search parameters that target only Patient; cited only as background for leaving ImagingStudy-patient Patient-scoped.
